operative_clauses.judgment_reason: EO 9618 (signed "September 19,1945.", Filed, Sept. 19, 1945) appoints Edwin G. Arnold as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, "vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned," to serve without additional compensation and to exercise the functions conferred by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, which "The said Executive orders are hereby" amended accordingly. EO 9901, signed "October 25, 1947." (12 FR 6965), appoints James P. Davis as Administrator, "vice Edwin G. Arnold, resigned, to serve" without additional compensation, gives him the functions conferred by the same four orders, and says that the said Executive orders are amended accordingly. EO 9901 therefore shows that Arnold had resigned and had been replaced no later than October 25, 1947, when the functions conferred on him were conferred on his successor. The date of Arnold's resignation is not held and may be earlier; October 25, 1947 is the latest date by which his appointment and functions had ended and the first date on which a held instrument documents the end, so it is recorded as the first end with that qualification. The appointing words were performed on signing, September 19, 1945; that earlier date is an alternative candidate for the end of the appointing act alone, but the clause also confers functions on the appointee during his service, which ended no later than October 25, 1947. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of EO 9901 (its provision quoted by the dossier's change record). EO 10018 (1948-11-15) and EO 10468 (1953-07-07) come after this end and do not alter it.

research_rationale:
EO 9618 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9618.txt, 10 FR 11931, PDF page 3); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order appoints Edwin G. Arnold, Director, Division of Territories and Island Possessions, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned, to serve without additional compensation, and to exercise the functions conferred on the Administration and the Administrator by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, which it amends accordingly. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The appointment is ended by a held successor order that appoints another Administrator 'vice' Arnold and amends the same four orders.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9618 by number. The dossier chain lists three later instruments naming the same office or its orders: EO 9901 (signed 1947-10-25, appoints Davis vice Arnold), EO 10018 (1948-11-15, transfers tracts of land from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of Agriculture; after the end) and EO 10468 (1953-07-07, appoints Strand vice Davis; after the end). The later-events catalog search recorded 4 machine hits and the name search 1 hit (EO 9901); no held text shows an earlier revocation, resignation date or supersession. The earliest held instrument showing that Arnold had resigned and been replaced is EO 9901. The order states no term, until-date or condition.","independent_command_check":"The direction to serve without additional compensation and the conferral of functions are conditions of the appointment held by the same person and end with it; the amendment of the four earlier orders 'accordingly' is the means by which the functions are conferred on the appointee and is replaced, for the successor, by the same words in EO 9901. No independent delegation, committee or report direction is present.","savings_check":"The functions were conferred on the individual appointee; EO 9901 re-conferred them on the successor in the same terms, so the residual is a transfer, not a surviving command of EO 9618. Acts done under the appointment before the successor are accrued; no held source shows any continuing command of this order.","scope_check":"One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9618#whole): the paragraph that appoints Arnold, directs that he serve without additional compensation and exercise the functions conferred by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. The recitals of authority (the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and the act of February 11, 1936) are not commands."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9901 conferred the same functions, duties and authority under Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 on James P. Davis, so what the order gave Arnold was transferred to his successor; acts done by Arnold as Administrator before then are accrued. No held source shows any continuing command of EO 9618 after that transfer.

research_rationale:
EO 9622 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9622.txt, 10 FR 12035, PDF page 3); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 9103 of March 18, 1942. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The Federal Register text prints the signature date "September 20, 1945." and the filing line "Filed, Sept. 21, 1945;". The sentence has no effective-date wording of its own, so the revocation took effect on signing, September 20, 1945. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

No earlier cessation is possible for a command to revoke another order that was performed when the order took effect. Neither the report-deadline rule nor the amendment rule applies: the order states no report date and no amendment.","independent_command_check":"The order has no appointment, delegation, committee, report direction or other command apart from the revocation of Executive Order 9103; the signature, date and Federal Register filing lines are not commands.","savings_check":"Acts done under Executive Order 9103 before its revocation are consequences of that other order, which this claim does not cover. This order creates no continuing right or duty, and no held source shows a residual command of EO 9622 after its date.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the single sentence that revokes Executive Order 9103 of March 18, 1942 (uniform control over the publication and use of Federal statistical information that would give aid and comfort to the enemy). The machine inventory (EO:9622#whole, the \"By virtue\" paragraph) is complete and correct; the heading and title are not commands. Doc. 45-17646) precedes the heading of EO 9622, so it does not govern EO 9622."}

The Federal Register text of the order prints the signature date "September 21, 1945." and the filing line "Filed, Sept. 24, 1945;". The command to revoke was performed, and so exhausted, on 1945-09-21. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself. No later instrument, amendment, extension or earlier event alters or ends the command: the dossier chain is empty and the order states no until-date, report date or condition.

research_rationale:
EO 9625 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9625.txt, 10 FR 12073, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 9294 of January 4, 1943. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The Federal Register text prints the signature date "September 21, 1945." and the filing line "Filed, Sept. 24, 1945;" and the issue date line "Washington, Tuesday, September 25, 1945". The sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, September 21, 1945. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9625 by number. The dossier chain for EO 9625 is empty and the later-events catalog search has no hit. No earlier cessation is possible for a command to revoke another order that was performed when the order took effect. Neither the report-deadline rule nor the amendment rule applies: the order states no report date and no amendment.","independent_command_check":"The order has no appointment, delegation, committee, report direction or other command apart from the revocation of Executive Order 9294; the signature, date and Federal Register filing lines are not commands.","savings_check":"Acts done under Executive Order 9294 before its revocation are consequences of that other order, which this claim does not cover. This order creates no continuing right or duty, and no held source shows a residual command of EO 9625 after its date.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the single paragraph that revokes Executive Order 9294 of January 4, 1943 (further defining the functions and duties of the Office of Defense Transportation). The machine inventory (EO:9625#whole, characters 781-982) stops after the words \"it is ordered that\" and omits the object and the words of revocation, so the inventory is corrected to the whole paragraph, characters 781-1145 of the registered text, ending \"be, and it is hereby, revoked.\" Nothing else in the order is a command."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, transfer or residual clause; it only revokes Executive Order 9294. The machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR (both as of the October 14, 2026 cutoff, edition caveats stated in their coverage notes) and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9625, so no held source continues any command of this order.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and the statutes, and 
as President of the United States and 
Commander in Chief of the Army and 
Navy of the United States, it is ordered 
as follows:
1. In accordance with Article II of the 
Charter of the International Military 
Tribunal established by the Government 
of the United States of America, the 
Provisional Government of the French 
Republic, the Government of the United 
Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern 
Ireland, and the Government of the 
Union of Soviet Socialist Republics for 
the trial and punishment of the major 
war criminals of the European Axis, pur­
suant to their agreement of August 8, 
1945, I hereby appoint Francis Biddle 
of Pennsylvania to be the Member for 
the United States of the International 
Military Tribunal and John J. Parker 
of North Carolina to be the Alternate 
Member for the United States, of the In­
ternational Military Tribunal.
2. The Member for the United States 
of the International Military Tribunal 
shall receive such compensation and al­
lowance for expenses as may be deter­
mined by the Secretary of State. The 
Alternate Member shall serve without 
compensation but shall receive such al­
lowance for expenses as may be author­
ized by the Secretary of State.

tary of War, the Attorney General, and 
the Secretary of the Navy are authorized 
to provide appropriate assistance to the 
Member and the Alternate Member in
the performance of their duties hereun­
der and may assign or detail such per­
sonnel, including members of the armed 
forces, as may be requested for the 
purpose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause amends paragraph 2 of EO 9611 to read "shall consist of the following members:" with a new list of three members, and provides: "The period of sixty days specified in" paragraph 1 of EO 9611 "begin to run on the date of this Order." (the words "paragraph 1  of the said Order, shall" lie between them). The signature date is "September 24, 1945." so the sixty days run from September 24, 1945. Counting September 24 as the first day, the sixtieth day is November 22, 1945; counting from the day after, the sixty days are complete on November 23, 1945. The recorded end is November 23, 1945 (the later reading). The new membership and the starting of the period operate only while the Board is re-established, so both end with the period. EO 9611 paragraph 1 also allows a shorter period for completion of the Board's functions; no held source dates an earlier completion. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. The commands of EO 9611 other than paragraph 2 and the period start are outside this clause.

research_rationale:
EO 9627 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9627.txt, 10 FR 12113, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order amends paragraph 2 of EO 9611 of September 10, 1945 (which re-established the Advisory Board on Just Compensation for sixty days) to name a new membership after Judge John J. Parker became unable to serve, and provides that the sixty-day period in paragraph 1 of EO 9611 begins to run on the date of this order. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The period of the Board's re-establishment is fixed by EO 9611 paragraph 1 and restarted by this order; the end below follows from this order's own sentence about the period.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The dossier chain for EO 9627 is empty, the later-events catalog search has no hit, and the packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9627 by number. The order's own sentence, \"The period of sixty days specified in\" paragraph 1 \"of the said Order\" shall begin to run on the date of this order, gives the end. EO 9611 allows an earlier end 'for such shorter period of time as may be required for the completion of its functions'; no held source shows that the Board completed its functions or was discharged earlier, so no earlier dated end is claimed. Neither a report deadline nor a later amendment ends the clause.","independent_command_check":"Both commands in the clause (membership of the Board as amended, and the start date of the sixty days) are tied to the existence of the Board and end with its period; neither is an appointment of a person to an office that outlasts the Board, a delegation or a report direction.","savings_check":"Nothing in the order or in a held source shows a residual duty or right of this order after the Board's period; the surviving question about paragraph 3 of EO 9611 is outside this order's text.","scope_check":"One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9627#whole): the amendment of paragraph 2 of EO 9611 (new membership) together with the sentence starting the sixty-day period. The recital that Judge Parker is unable to serve is not a command. The order amends only paragraph 2 and the start of the period; it leaves paragraphs 1 and 3 of EO 9611 otherwise as they were."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings or transfer clause. Its two commands (the new membership of the Board and the start of the sixty-day period) have no residual effect once the Board's period ended, and the machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9627. Whether the direction in paragraph 3 of EO 9611 that the War Shipping Administration be guided by the Board's determination survived the Board's period concerns EO 9611, not this order, and is not decided here.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9670
E stablishing  the  T ennessee  N ational  
W ild life R efuge
WHEREAS on November 29, 1945, the 
Tennessee Valley Authority and the 
United States Department of the Interior 
entered into an agreement providing for 
the transfer by the Authority to the De­
partment of certain rights with respect 
to the lands therein designated and de­
scribed in the counties of Henry, Ben­
ton, Humphreys, and Decatur, Tennessee, 
so that such lands might be reserved and 
used as a wildlife refuge, in accordance 
with the terms and conditions of the 
agreement and subject to my approval of 
the agreement and my establishment of 
the contemplated refuge; and 
WHEREAS I have this day approved 
the said agreement between the Tennes­
see Valley Authority and the United 
States Department of the Interior; and 
WHEREAS it appears that the estab­
lishment of the wildlife refuge contem­
plated by the agreement will further the 
purposes of the Migratory Bird Conser­
vation Act (45 Stat. 1222) and is in the 
public interest:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me as President of 
the United States, I  hereby reserve and 
set apart for the use of the Department 
of the Interior as a refuge and wildlife 
management area for migratory birds 
and other wildlife the lands designated 
and described for that purpose in the 
said agreement of November 29,1945, be­
tween the Tennessee Valley Authority 
and the United States Department of the 
Interior, such reservation to be in ac­
cordance with, and subject to, the terms 
and conditions of the said agreement.
This reservation shall be known as the 
Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge.
H arry  S. T r um an
T h e W h it e H o u se,
December 28, 1945.
[F. R. Doc. 45-23162; Filed, Dec. 29, 1945;
12:25 p. m.] /

The Federal Register text of the order prints the signature date "December 28, 1945" and the filing line "Filed, Dec. 29, 1945;". The command to revoke was performed, and so exhausted, on 1945-12-28. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself. No later instrument, amendment, extension or earlier event alters or ends the command: the dossier chain is empty and the order states no until-date, report date or condition.

research_rationale:
EO 9667 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9667.txt, 11 FR 4, PDF page 4); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 9074 of February 25, 1942. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The Federal Register text prints the signature date "December 28, 1945" and the filing line "Filed, Dec. 29, 1945;". The sentence ending "hereby revoked." has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, December 28, 1945. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

The dossier chain for EO 9667 is empty and the later-events catalog search has no hit. No earlier cessation is possible for a command to revoke another order that was performed when the order took effect. Neither the report-deadline rule nor the amendment rule applies: the order states no report date and no amendment.","independent_command_check":"The order has no appointment, delegation, committee, report direction or other command apart from the revocation of Executive Order 9074; the signature, date and Federal Register filing lines are not commands.","savings_check":"Acts done under Executive Order 9074 before its revocation are consequences of that other order, which this claim does not cover. This order creates no continuing right or duty, and no held source shows a residual command of EO 9667 after its date.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the single sentence that revokes Executive Order 9074 of February 25, 1942 (directing the Secretary of the Navy to take action necessary to protect vessels, harbors, ports and waterfront facilities). The last section of the preceding order, which makes that order effective as of the opening of business January 28, 1946, is printed before the heading of EO 9667; its signature line (December 27, 1945) precedes this order's heading, so it does not govern EO 9667."}

WHEREAS on November 29, 1945, the 
Tennessee Valley Authority and the 
United States Department of the Interior 
entered into an agreement providing for

partment of certain rights with respect 
to the lands therein designated and de­
scribed in the counties of Henry, Ben­

used as a wildlife refuge, in accordance 
with the terms and conditions of the 
agreement and subject to my approval of 
the agreement and my establishment of 
the contemplated refuge; and 
WHEREAS I have this day approved 
the said agreement between the Tennes­
see Valley Authority and the United 
States Department of the Interior; and

lishment of the wildlife refuge contem­
plated by the agreement will further the 
purposes of the Migratory Bird Conser­
vation Act (45 Stat. 1222) and is in the

and described for that purpose in the 
said agreement of November 29,1945, be­
tween the Tennessee Valley Authority 
and the United States Department of the 
Interior, such reservation to be in ac­
cordance with, and subject to, the terms 
and conditions of the said agreement.

Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 1 closes the departments and agencies one-half day on Tuesday, December 24, 1946, the day preceding Christmas Day, and excuses employees from duty; its words are "be excused from duty for one-half day" and "on December 24, 1946." The command is confined by its own terms to that one day, so it was performed, and exhausted, on December 24, 1946. The end is recorded as December 24, 1946, the whole day (inclusive); the exclusive reading would have the command end when that day begins, with no change in substance because the half-day closure is the performance of the command. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. No amendment, extension or revocation is held, and the dossier chain is empty.

research_rationale:
EO 9810 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9810.txt, 11 FR 14303, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order has two numbered sections: section 1 closes the Federal agencies one-half day on Tuesday, December 24, 1946, and excuses employees; section 2 directs publication in the Federal Register. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms confine its only substantive command to one named day.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The dossier chain for EO 9810 is empty and the later-events catalog search has no hit. The packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9810 by number. The order's own terms give the end: the closure and excusal are for \"December 24, 1946\" only. The excusal could not have ended before it began, and no held text revokes, amends or extends it. An until-date is recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading stated in the clause reason (owner ruling 2026-10-21).","independent_command_check":"Section 2 (publication) is independent of section 1 in time: it was performed when the order appeared in the Federal Register, before December 24, 1946. Neither section creates an appointment, delegation, report direction or continuing duty.","savings_check":"The excusal of employees on the half day is a completed consequence; nothing in the order or in a held source continues it after December 24, 1946. The exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with law are part of section 1 and end with it.","scope_check":"Two operative clauses, matching the machine inventory (EO:9810#1 and EO:9810#2): section 1 (closure and excusal for the half day) and section 2 (publication). The heading and recitals are not commands and the machine inventory is complete and correct."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, transfer or residual clause, and no continuing right or duty: it excused employees from duty for one-half day on December 24, 1946 only. The machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9810, so no held source continues any command of this order.

WHEREAS the Alaska Railroad is the 
only means by which substantial quan­
tities of vitally needed materials and 
supplies can be transported to interior

and most effective utilization of this lim­

and mechanics employed by the Govern­

gency; and

foregoing an extraordinary emergency 
exists:

authority vested in me by section 1  of 
the said act of August 1, 1892, as 
amended by the said act of March 3, 
1913, and as President of the United 
States, I  hereby suspend for a period of 
six months, effective immediately, the
above-mentioned provisions of law pro­
hibiting more than eight hours of labor 
in any one day by laborers and mechan­
ics employed by the Government of the 
United States as to all work performed 
by laborers and mechanics employed by

Interior, on any public work within the 
Territory of Alaska with respect to which 
the Secretary of the Interior shall find 
such suspension to be essential to the 
accomplishment of the purposes of this 
order: Provided, That the wages of all 
laborers and mechanics so employed by 
the Alaska. Railroad shall be based on an 
administrative workweek of forty hours 
with overtime to be paid at time and 
one-half for all hours of work in ex­
cess of forty hours in any such admin­
istrative workweek.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause states "hereby suspend for a period of" and, on the next line, "six months, effective immediately, the" eight-hour provisions for the Alaska Railroad work described. The signature date is "May 9,1947" and the filing line reads "Filed, May 9, 1947;", so the suspension began on May 9, 1947 and the six months were complete on November 9, 1947. The recorded end is November 9, 1947 (the later reading); counting May 9 as the first day would make November 8, 1947 the last day of the six months. The proviso that wages be based on a forty-hour administrative workweek with "with overtime to be paid at time and" one-half (the line break follows 'and') is part of the same paragraph and is limited to work under the suspension. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. The six months are the order's own fixed term, not a report deadline; no later order extends or revokes the suspension, and no held finding of the Secretary of the Interior ends it sooner.

EO 9849 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9849.txt, 12 FR 3071, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order suspends, for six months from May 9, 1947, the eight-hour-day limit of the act of August 1, 1892 as amended by the act of March 3, 1913 (40 U.S.C. 321) for work by laborers and mechanics of the Alaska Railroad, Department of the Interior, on public work in Alaska that the Secretary of the Interior finds essential, with a proviso on wages and overtime. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms fix the period of the suspension.

The order states its own period, \"six months, effective immediately\", from the signature and filing date May 9, 1947. The suspension applies only to work for which the Secretary of the Interior finds it essential; no held finding or order withdraws it earlier, and an earlier withdrawal is not shown by any held source. The period is the fixed term of the order, not a report deadline, and no amendment or extension is held.","independent_command_check":"The proviso on wages and overtime applies only to work performed under the suspension and has no life apart from it. The order contains no appointment, delegation, report direction or other independent command.","savings_check":"Accrued wage and overtime entitlements for work done during the six months survive as consequences of the suspension; the order contains no other savings or transfer language and no held source shows any continuing command after the term.","scope_check":"One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9849#whole): the paragraph that suspends the eight-hour provisions for six months and carries the wage and overtime proviso. research_rationale:
EO 9859 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9859.txt, 12 FR 3557, PDF page 3); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 9196 of July 9, 1942. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The Federal Register text prints the signature date "May 31,1947." and a filing line with the filing date June 2, 1947. The sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, May 31, 1947 (filed June 2, 1947). Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause, the paragraph beginning "NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the", orders Executive Order 9172 of May 22, 1942 (establishing a panel for the creation of emergency boards for the adjustment of railway labor disputes) revoked, in words that read "be, and it is hereby," and then, on the next line, "revoked." The Federal Register text prints the signature date "August 11, 1947." and a filing line whose date is August 11, 1947. The sentence has no effective-date wording, so the command to revoke was performed, and so exhausted, on signing, August 11, 1947. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself. No later instrument, amendment, extension or earlier event alters or ends the command: the dossier chain is empty and the order states no until-date, report date or condition.

research_rationale:
EO 9883 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9883.txt, 12 FR 5481, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 9172 of May 22, 1942. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The Federal Register text prints the signature date "August 11, 1947." and a filing line with the filing date August 11, 1947. The operative sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, August 11, 1947. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

The dossier chain for EO 9883 is empty and the later-events catalog search has no hit. No earlier cessation is possible for a command to revoke another order that was performed when the order took effect. Neither the report-deadline rule nor the amendment rule applies: the order states no report date and no amendment.","independent_command_check":"The order has no appointment, delegation, committee, report direction or other command apart from the revocation of Executive Order 9172; the signature, date and Federal Register filing lines are not commands.","savings_check":"Acts done under Executive Order 9172 before its revocation are consequences of that other order, which this claim does not cover. This order creates no continuing right or duty, and no held source shows a residual command of EO 9883 after its date.","scope_check":"One operative clause: the paragraph beginning \"NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the\" that orders Executive Order 9172 of May 22, 1942 (establishing a panel for the creation of emergency boards for the adjustment of railway labor disputes) revoked. The two recitals before it (that Order 9172 established a panel for the duration of the war and six months thereafter, and that the procedures under the Railway Labor Act are now adequate) are findings, not separate commands. The machine inventory (EO:9883#whole) is complete and correct. The sentence \"Effective upon publication in the F ed­\" near the end of the held text is the lead-in of a Civil Service Commission regulation printed after the order, not part of it."}

Washington, Saturday, August 30, J  947
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9889 \
R estricting  C o m petitio n to  V eterans  in
E x am in atio n for  the  P o s it io n of S u b­
stitute  R a il w a y P ostal  C lerk
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the statutes, including section 2 of the 
Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403), the Vet­
erans’ Preference Act of 1944, approved  
June 27,1944 (58 Stat. 387), and section 
1753 of the Revised Statutes of the  
United States (5 U. S. C. 631), it is hereby 
ordered as follows:
In civil service examinations for the'  
position of Substitute Railway Postal  
Clerk competition shall be restricted, un­
til July 25, 1952, to persons entitled to  
preference under the said Veterans’ Pref­
erence Act of 1944, as long as persons  
entitled to preference are available: Pro­
vided, however,  that for purposes of  
classification application for examination 
may be accepted by the Civil Service  
Commission from any person who has  
been serving in such position continu­
ously since the date of this order under  
an appointment not limited to one year  
or less, and the Commission is authorized 
to confer a competitive civil service status 
or a probational status upon any such  
employee who qualifies in the examina­
tion for classification: And provided fur­
ther, that in no event shall any person  
not entitled to preference under the Vet­
erans’ Preference Act of 1944 be granted  
a competitive civil service status or a  
probational status under this order (1)  
unless he is recommended for this pur­
pose by the Postmaster General and (2)  
until all preference eligibles who have  
the same or a higher rating in the ex­
amination have been appointed or have 
been given consideration in accordance  
with the Veterans’ Preference Act of 1944.
Incumbents of positions to which this  
order is applicable who do not have a  
competitive status and who fail to qual­
ify for a competitive civil service status  
or a probational status under this order 
shall be'replaced by selection from the  
competitive register in accordance with  
regulations prescribed by the Civil Serv­
ice Commission.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause restricts competition in examinations for Substitute Railway Postal Clerk, in the words that run "July 25, 1952, to persons" entitled to preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944, "as long as" persons so entitled are available. The order's own end date is July 25, 1952. It is recorded inclusive, so the restriction runs through the end of July 25, 1952; the exclusive reading would have it end when that day begins, so that July 24, 1952 is the last day. The second paragraph, which directs replacement of incumbents who fail to qualify, depends on the order being applicable and ends with the restriction. The signature date is "August 28, 1947." and the order is not conditioned on any act that could have ended it sooner except the availability of preference eligibles, which no held source dates. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. No held text extends, amends or revokes it.

research_rationale:
EO 9889 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9889.txt, 12 FR 5831, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order restricts competition in civil service examinations for the position of Substitute Railway Postal Clerk to persons entitled to veterans' preference under the Veterans' Preference Act of 1944 until July 25, 1952, as long as persons entitled to preference are available, with provisos on classification and on status for non-preference employees, and directs replacement of incumbents who do not qualify. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms fix the date to which the restriction runs.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The dossier chain for EO 9889 is empty, the later-events catalog search has no hit, and the packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds one other file citing EO 9889, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_9889.txt, which is the order's own Federal Register page text, not a later instrument. The order states its own end, \"July 25, 1952\". The restriction applies \"as long as\" preference-eligible persons are available; whether and when that condition failed is not shown by any held source, so it supplies no earlier dated end. The until-date is recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading stated in the clause reason (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No held text extends, amends or revokes the order.","independent_command_check":"The direction that incumbents without competitive status who fail to qualify be replaced by selection from the competitive register is attached to positions 'to which this order is applicable' and has no stated date of its own; it operates only while the restriction applies and so ends with it. The proviso on classification applications and the proviso on status for non-preference persons are conditions on the same restriction. The order contains no appointment, delegation or report direction.","savings_check":"Status conferred on a qualifying incumbent while the order was in force is an accrued consequence; the order contains no transfer or savings clause for the restriction itself, and no held source shows the restriction or replacement direction continuing after its date.","scope_check":"One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9889#whole): the paragraph that restricts competition until July 25, 1952 (with its two provisos) and the following paragraph that directs replacement of incumbents who fail to qualify. The introductory sentence is the authority recital, not a command."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order authorized the Civil Service Commission to confer a competitive civil service status or a probational status on a qualifying incumbent who had served continuously since the date of the order; status so conferred before the restriction ended is an accrued consequence. No held source continues the restriction or the replacement direction after July 25, 1952.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: EO 9901 (signed "October 25, 1947.") appoints James P. Davis as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, "vice Edwin G. Arnold, resigned, to serve" without additional compensation and to exercise the functions conferred by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, which "The said Executive orders are hereby" amended accordingly. EO 10468, signed "July 7,1953." (18 FR, issue of July 9, 1953), appoints William C. Strand as Administrator, "James P. Davis, resigned, to serve with" the same terms, gives him the functions conferred by the same four orders, and amends them accordingly. EO 10468 therefore shows that Davis had resigned and had been replaced no later than July 7, 1953, when the functions conferred on him were conferred on his successor. The date of Davis's resignation is not held and may be earlier; July 7, 1953 is the latest date by which his appointment and functions had ended and the first date on which a held instrument documents the end, so it is recorded as the first end with that qualification. The appointing words were performed on signing, October 25, 1947; that earlier date is an alternative candidate for the end of the appointing act alone, but the clause also confers functions on the appointee during his service. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of EO 10468 (its provision quoted by the dossier's change record). EO 10018 (1948-11-15) is not an end of this clause.

research_rationale:
EO 9901 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9901.txt, 12 FR 6965, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order appoints James P. Davis, Director, Division of Territories and Island Possessions, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice Edwin G. Arnold, resigned, to serve without additional compensation, and to exercise the functions conferred on the Administration and the Administrator by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, which it amends accordingly. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The appointment is ended by a held successor order that appoints another Administrator 'vice' Davis and amends the same four orders.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds one other file citing EO 9901, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_9901.txt, which is the order's own Federal Register page text, not a later instrument. The dossier chain lists EO 10018 (1948-11-15, transfers tracts of land between departments; it neither names Davis nor ends the appointment) and EO 10468 (1953-07-07, appoints Strand vice Davis). The later-events catalog search recorded 1 machine hit and the name search 1 hit (EO 10468); no held text shows an earlier revocation, resignation date or supersession. The earliest held instrument showing that Davis had resigned and been replaced is EO 10468. The order states no term, until-date or condition.","independent_command_check":"The direction to serve without additional compensation and the conferral of functions are conditions of the appointment held by the same person and end with it; the amendment of the four earlier orders 'accordingly' is the means by which the functions are conferred on the appointee and is repeated for his successor in EO 10468. No independent delegation, committee or report direction is present.","savings_check":"The functions were conferred on the individual appointee; EO 10468 re-conferred them on the successor in the same terms, so the residual is a transfer, not a surviving command of EO 9901. Acts done under the appointment before the successor are accrued; no held source shows any continuing command of this order.","scope_check":"One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9901#whole): the paragraph that appoints Davis, directs that he serve without additional compensation and exercise the functions conferred by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. The recitals of authority are not commands."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10468 conferred the same functions, duties and authority under Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 on William C. Strand, so what the order gave Davis was transferred to his successor; acts done by Davis as Administrator before then are accrued. No held source shows any continuing command of EO 9901 after that transfer.

The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself. No later instrument, amendment, extension or earlier event alters or ends the command: the dossier chain is empty and the order states no until-date, report date or condition.

research_rationale:
EO 9906 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9906.txt, 12 FR 7799, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order's one operative sentence revokes Executive Order 7165 of August 29, 1935. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The sentence "This order shall become effective upon" its filing for publication fixes the date by the filing line, which reads "Filed, Nov. 18, 1947;"; the signature date is "November 18, 1947." as well, so the revocation took effect on November 18, 1947. Under owner ruling 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) a command that was performed on its date is recorded as exhausted by performance on that date.

Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES  
OF AMERICA 
A  PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS by the act of Congress ap­
proved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the  
President is authorized, under the con­
ditions prescribed in that act, to grant  
an extension of time for the fulfillment  
of the conditions and formalities for the  
renewal of trade-mark registrations pre­
scribed by section 12 of the act author­
izing the registration of trade-marks  
used in commerce with foreign nations  
or among the several States or with In­
dian tribes, and protecting the same,  
approved February 20, 1905, as amended 
(15 U. S. C. 92), by nationals of coun­
tries which accord substantially equal  
treatment in this respect to citizens of  
the United States of America:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, HARRY S.  
TRUMAN, President of the United States 
of America, under and by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by the aforesaid  
act of July 17,1946, do find and proclaim 
that with respect to trade-marks of na­
tionals of Luxembourg registered in the  
United States Patent Office which have  
been subject tç renewal on or after Sep­
tember 3, 1939, there has existed during  
several years since that date, because of  
conditions growing out of World War II,  
such disruption or suspension of facilities  
essential to compliance with the condi­
tions and formalities prescribed with re­
spect to renewal of such registrations by  
section 12 of the aforesaid act of Febru­
ary 20, 1905, as amended, as to bring  
such registrations within thé terms of  
the aforesaid act of July 17, 1946; that  
Luxembourg accords substantially equal  
treatment in this respect to trade-mark  
proprietors who are citizens of the  
United States; and that accordingly the  
time within which compliance with con­
ditions and formalities prescribed with
respect to renewal of registrations un­
der section 12 of the aforesaid act of  
February 20,1905, as amended, may take  
place is hereby extended with respect to  
such registrations which expired after  
September 3, 1939, and before June 30,  
1947, until and including June 30, 1948,
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have here­
unto set my hand and caused the Seal of  
the United States of America to be  
affixed.
DONE at the City of Washington this  
21st day of January, in the year of our  
Lord nineteen hundred and  
[seal ] forty-eight, and of the Inde­
pendence of the United States  
of America the one hundred and seventy-  
second.
H arry S. T ruman

The order has two numbered sections: section 1 suspends the operation of all provisions of law requiring professional examinations for permanent promotion of Regular Army officers of the Medical, Dental and Veterinary Corps until June 30, 1948, and section 2 makes the order effective as of January 1, 1948. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The order states its own end, \"until June 30,1948.\" The until-date is recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading stated in the clause reason (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No held text extends, amends or revokes the suspension, and the order states no condition that ends it earlier.","independent_command_check":"Section 2 only dates the order (effective as of January 1, 1948, three weeks before the January 21, 1948 signature) and carries no command of its own; the suspension of section 1 is the only substantive command. TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
PROCLAMATION 2766

mark R egistrations :  Luxembourg
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES  
OF AMERICA 
A  PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS by the act of Congress ap­
proved July 17, 1946, 60 Stat. 568, the  
President is authorized, under the con­
ditions prescribed in that act, to grant  
an extension of time for the fulfillment  
of the conditions and formalities for the  
renewal of trade-mark registrations pre­
scribed by section 12 of the act author­
izing the registration of trade-marks  
used in commerce with foreign nations  
or among the several States or with In­
dian tribes, and protecting the same,  
approved February 20, 1905, as amended 
(15 U. S. C. 92), by nationals of coun­
tries which accord substantially equal  
treatment in this respect to citizens of  
the United States of America:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, HARRY S.  
TRUMAN, President of the United States 
of America, under and by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by the aforesaid  
act of July 17,1946, do find and proclaim 
that with respect to trade-marks of na­
tionals of Luxembourg registered in the  
United States Patent Office which have  
been subject tç renewal on or after Sep­
tember 3, 1939, there has existed during  
several years since that date, because of  
conditions growing out of World War II,  
such disruption or suspension of facilities  
essential to compliance with the condi­
tions and formalities prescribed with re­
spect to renewal of such registrations by  
section 12 of the aforesaid act of Febru­
ary 20, 1905, as amended, as to bring  
such registrations within thé terms of  
the aforesaid act of July 17, 1946; that  
Luxembourg accords substantially equal  
treatment in this respect to trade-mark  
proprietors who are citizens of the  
United States; and that accordingly the  
time within which compliance with con­
ditions and formalities prescribed with
respect to renewal of registrations un­
der section 12 of the aforesaid act of  
February 20,1905, as amended, may take  
place is hereby extended with respect to  
such registrations which expired after  
September 3, 1939, and before June 30,  
1947, until and including June 30, 1948,
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have here­
unto set my hand and caused the Seal of  
the United States of America to be  
affixed.
DONE at the City of Washington this  
21st day of January, in the year of our  
Lord nineteen hundred and  
[seal ] forty-eight, and of the Inde­
pendence of the United States  
of America the one hundred and seventy-  
second.
H arry S. T ruman
By the President:
G. C. M arshall ,
Secretary of State.

in  the  M edical D epartment  of the  
Army
By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by section 507 (b) of the Officer Per­
sonnel Act of 1947, approved August 7,  
1947 (Public Law 381, 80th Congress), it  
is ordered as follows:
1. The operation of all provisions of  
law requiring professional examinations  
for permanent promotion in the Regular  
Army of officers of the-Medical, Dental,  
and Veterinary Corps is hereby suspend­
ed until June 30,1948.
2. This order shall become effective as  
of January 1,1948.
H arry 8 . Truman
